title: Ultrasound modes used in fetal echocardiography

items.question: Which three modalities should every fetal echocardiogram use together?
options: Two-dimensional imaging, colour Doppler and spectral Doppler
M-mode, continuous-wave Doppler and strain imaging
items.explanation: Two-dimensional, colour Doppler and spectral Doppler imaging are used together, with settings optimised for the fetal heart.

items.question: Which set of modes is the minimum a machine needs for fetal echocardiography?
options: B-mode, M-mode, colour flow and pulsed-wave Doppler
B-mode, continuous-wave Doppler and tissue Doppler
items.explanation: The minimum is two-dimensional (B-mode), M-mode, colour flow and pulsed-wave Doppler.

items.question: You want the flow pattern at one exact point, such as the ductus venosus. Which mode?
items.explanation: Pulsed-wave Doppler gives the flow profile and direction at a chosen site.

items.question: When is continuous-wave Doppler needed?
options: When flow is abnormally fast, to measure high velocities and gradients
To time atrial and ventricular contraction
To show small veins with slow flow
items.explanation: It is not needed for a normal heart. It characterises high velocities and gradients and helps estimate pressure from a regurgitant jet.

items.question: What does power Doppler display?
options: The amplitude of the Doppler signal
The frequency shift of the Doppler signal
Movement of one line of tissue over time
items.explanation: Power Doppler shows signal amplitude rather than frequency shift, which makes it useful for small vessels and slow flow.

items.question: Where do you place the M-mode cursor to work out a rhythm?
options: Through an atrial wall and a ventricular free wall together
items.explanation: Crossing an atrial and a ventricular wall puts both contractions on one trace, so their timing can be compared.

items.question: Which pair of flows, sampled together with pulsed-wave Doppler, shows atrial and ventricular timing on one trace?
options: Superior vena cava and ascending aorta
Middle cerebral artery and ductus venosus
Right and left branch pulmonary arteries
items.explanation: Recognised pairs are superior vena cava with ascending aorta, mitral inflow with aortic outflow, and pulmonary artery with pulmonary vein.

items.question: The fetal heart rhythm is irregular. What should the examination record?
options: The mechanism, using M-mode, pulsed-wave Doppler or tissue Doppler
Nothing further if the four-chamber view is normal
items.explanation: With an irregular, slow or fast rhythm, the mechanism should be documented using one or more of these modes.

items.question: How should the beam lie for a pulsed-wave Doppler recording?
options: Along the flow, or within 20 degrees of it
At right angles to the flow
At 45 to 60 degrees to the flow
items.explanation: Align with the flow or keep within 20 degrees, with a small sample gate.

items.question: Which of these is a required pulsed-wave Doppler site in a fetal echocardiogram?
items.explanation: Required sites include the umbilical vein, ductus venosus, pulmonary veins, both inflows, both outflows, the distal ductus arteriosus and the umbilical artery. The others listed here are optional.

items.question: What is the current standing of STIC in fetal echocardiography?
options: It can add information but is not validated for clinical use
It is required in every examination
It is used only to measure heart rate
items.explanation: Three-dimensional imaging and STIC can add anatomical and functional detail, but STIC has not been validated for clinical use.

items.question: What frame rate is recommended for grey-scale imaging of the fetal heart?
items.explanation: Above 30 to 40 Hz, and 80 to 100 Hz may be needed for fast heart rates or speckle tracking.

items.question: In early pregnancy, what limit applies to the thermal and mechanical indices?
options: 1.0 or less, with Doppler used sparingly
No limit applies before the second trimester
3.0 or less if the scan is short
items.explanation: Keep both indices at or below 1.0, limit Doppler and keep exposure short.

items.question: In a routine mid-pregnancy cardiac screen, what is the place of colour Doppler?
items.explanation: Colour is not mandatory for screening; becoming familiar with it and adding it to routine screening is encouraged.

items.question: Which transducer type is preferred for fetal echocardiography?
items.explanation: Curvilinear probes are preferred; linear and sector probes may also be used.
